subject: Synthesis: cross-provider signals and next qualification steps
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Luke Reynolds <luke@atlasai.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Synthesis: cross-provider signals and next qualification steps

Thanks again for the call this morning, Luke — good to meet the Atlas team and hear more about your embedding/semantic search use case and the latency targets you mentioned (p95 < 220ms for 1–2k qps). Per our discussion, I captured the signals that will matter for qualification and sketched a short plan to validate: 

- Primary goals: 1) match or beat current throughput/latency at 1k qps; 2) hold MRR-relevant quality (<=3% hallucination on entity extraction prompts); 3) ensure PKI/KMS fit for your compliance needs.
- Differentiators to prove: prefix/KV caching win on repeated conversational context, cost delta when using Redwood batching vs Atlas’ current hyperscaler endpoint, and graceful fallback to smaller quantized variants under load.

Next concrete steps I propose (I can own scheduling):
1) You share the minimal prompt set and 20 representative queries (we can anonymize) — we attached a starter prompt-suite (prompt-suite-v1.txt) and the redwood_eval_matrix.xlsx to show test vectors.
2) We run an apples-to-apples run across three configs: your current hyperscaler endpoint (what you run today), Redwood hosted default model, and Redwood with aggressive batching + KV caching.
3) We provide a short report with: latency distribution, hallucination counts on the probe prompts, token cost per 1k qps, and a short set of signal plots.

Attachments: redwood_eval_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet), prompt-suite-v1.txt (text) — also shared a Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-atlas-eval

Would you be comfortable sending the 20 sample queries and the hyperscaler endpoint test key (read-only) by EOD Friday? If not, we can run using a sandboxed mirror on our side — either works.

Thanks — I’ll block time for the runs next week once we have samples.

Best,
Grace
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: redwood_eval_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet)
Attachment: prompt-suite-v1.txt (text)
From: Luke Reynolds <luke@atlasai.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Atlas AI (procurement) <procurement@atlasai.com>
Date: Thu, 9 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Synthesis: cross-provider signals and next qualification steps

Grace — thanks for the clear write-up. Quick clarifications from our side: 

- We can send 20 de-identified queries by tomorrow morning.
- Our hyperscaler endpoint owner will provide a read-only token but it may take procurement sign-off (looping them).
- Two priority probes for us: named-entity precision on product descriptions and hallucination frequency when asked sourcing-origin questions (we frequently see provenance hallucinations).

One ask: can you include a smoke check for response determinism for short prompts (we have a requirement for top-1 stability across repeated calls for specific billing statements)?

Also copying procurement — they may ask about data retention and audit logs (SOC2) before sharing the token.

—Luke
Head of Product
Atlas AI

Appreciate the quick turnaround, Luke. Confirming team plan based on your notes: 

- We’ll include a determinism smoke check (5 repeated calls per short prompt, compare token-level deltas and top-1 answer stability).
- We’ll add a small provenance/hallucination probe focusing on sourcing-origin for the product descriptions you flagged.
- If procurement needs SOC2 artifacts before token exchange, we can send the SOC2 letter + retention/audit notes (link below).

Operational timeline: 
- Fri 9/10: we’ll ingest your 20 de-identified queries once you drop them in the Drive folder.
- Mon 9/13: run batch jobs across three configs (your hyperscaler token pending; if procurement delays, we’ll fake the endpoint with recorded traces and note it).
- Tue 9/14: deliver short report + 2-slide exec summary and a table of the top 10 hallucination examples.

I attached an updated eval matrix (redwood_eval_matrix.xlsx) with the determinism columns filled in and a stub procurement packet: atlas-procurement-questions.pdf.

If that timeline looks good, I’ll create a mutual action plan in HubSpot and schedule a 30-min demo for Friday to show the caching/batching dashboard live.

Thanks,
Grace
